messages.subject: Re: async in Rhipe 0.73?
parts:
I know you can do
job = rhwatch(..., noeval=TRUE)
rhex(job, async=TRUE)

With noeval=TRUE, rhwatch is basically rhmr with new arguments.


On Wednesday, May 29, 2013 8:46:36 PM UTC-7, Philip Gautier wrote:
Does Rhipe 0.73 have an option similar to async = FALSE?  I have many Rhipe jobs to be submitted in a for loop, and I would prefer to submit them one at a time so that I don't tie up resources for other users on the cluster.

Thanks,
Philip

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] async in Rhipe 0.73?
parts:
As of 0.73, this is the correct way (see definition of mon.sec in ?rhstatus)

## Will wait till job is complete
z1 <- rhwatch(map=function(a,b) NULL,reduce=0, input=c(10,1),mon.sec=Inf)

## Run several jobs (at once)  and wait for all to complete
jobs <- list()
jobs[[1]] <- rhwatch(map=function(a,b) 1,reduce=0, input=c(10,1),mon.sec=0,read=FALSE)
jobs[[2]] <- rhwatch(map=function(a,b) 1,reduce=0, input=c(10,1),mon.sec=0,read=FALSE)
for(ajob in jobs){
  res <- rhstatus(ajob,mon.sec=Inf)
  print(sprintf("Job: is complete",res$jobname))
}
